newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel seeks offers for Bank Hapoalim.
newsitem.headline: Israel seeks offers for Bank Hapoalim.

text.p: The Israeli government published a notice on Tuesday seeking applications for the purchase of a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim, Israel's biggest commercial bank.
The announcement, published by the Treasury and M.I. Holdings, the government company charged with selling shares of state-owned banks, said applicants had until April 18 to register.
The government, which owns 78 percent of Hapoalim, said it hoped to complete the sale by mid-August. The offer is for between 25 percent and 69.3 percent of the bank.
The announcement marked the government's second attempt to sell Hapoalim after an effort launched in December 1994 ended without any formal offers.
"Recently M.I. Holdings received inquiries from two groups interested in presenting proposals for purchasing a bloc of shares from among those held by the state in the bank," the announcement said.
"Therefore M.I. Holdings and the government decided to reopen the sale process," it said.
The two groups are being formed by U.S. banker Jeffrey Keil and by U.S.-Israeli entrepreneur Ted Arison. The announcement said other groups were welcome to submit proposals as well.
Interested parties must show proof of financial ability to buy the shares and to meet the conditions for a banking licence set by the Bank of Israel.
Applicants will be required to deposit $40 million, the announcement said.

"M.I. Holdings and the government have established a timetable and framework whose goal is to bring about a signing of a sales contract if the proper conditions are created within a period of time of approximately four months from the last date for filing applications," the announcement said.
